newsitem.title: NETHERLANDS: Nedlloyd sees greater P&O container merger savings.
newsitem.headline: Nedlloyd sees greater P&O container merger savings.

text.p: Dutch shipping and road transport group Nedlloyd said on Wednesday the merger of its container business with that of Britain's P&O was ahead of schedule and would lead to greater synergy savings than the two parent companies had originally forecast.
Nedlloyd said the savings would largely fall in later quarters and that the P&O Nedlloyd container joint venture had made a loss in the first quarter of 1997 as it had expected.

"Container revenue rates have continued to reduce as anticipated in Q1 1997 but are starting to show signs of stability and the overall outlook is beginning to look more positive," it said in a statement.

P&O Nedlloyd was created when The Peninsular and Oriental Steam Navigation Co Plc and Koninklijke Nedlloyd Groep NV merged their container shipping businesses at the end of 1996, each taking a 50 percent stake in the new company.

In the first quarter of 1997 P&O Nedlloyd made a loss of $31 million before interest and other items, merger costs and tax. After interest and other items but before merger costs and tax the first-quarter loss came to $42 million.
"Progress is ahead of schedule for merging the previous businesses into the new company. On an annualised basis, savings of $200 million will be achieved by Q4 1997," Nedlloyd said.
Merger costs would mainly occur in the second, third and fourth quarters of 1997 with synergy savings increasing through 1997 and into 1998, it said.
"Total annual synergy will comfortably exceed the $200 million originally forecast, primarily through procurement, operational synergies and IT (information technology) systems."

Container shipping volumes and load factors were slightly higher in the first quarter of 1997 than in the same period of 1996 and volumes were expected to continue growing this year, leading effectively to full capacity utilisation, it said.
However, the erosion of freight rates experienced in 1996 continued into 1997, though signs of stability had begun to emerge by the end of the first quarter.
"Based on the current rate developments in ocean shipping, we expect P&O Nedlloyd to contribute positively to the 1997 Nedlloyd result," Nedlloyd added.
